item.title: Middle East live: Trump says he won’t 'be much more patient’ with Iran
item.description: US President Donald Trump ​said he would not be ​much ‌more ⁠patient with ‌Iran as he urged Tehran ⁠to reach a deal ​with Washington. Follow our liveblog for the latest developments in the Middle East.

item.title: Why did Saudi Arabia and the UAE allegedly carry out secret bombing raids on Iran?
item.description: The United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia in April secretly carried out a series of air strikes against Iran during the US-Israeli war against Tehran, the Wall Street Journal and Reuters reported this week. Analysts say these raids – which neither country has confirmed – would have been clandestine counterattacks following Tehran’s drone and missile strikes against Gulf state infrastructure.

item.title: Iran accuses United Arab Emirates of being 'active partner' in US-Israeli war
item.description: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi accused the United Arab Emirates on Thursday of playing an active role in the US-Israeli war against his country. Araghchi also referred to what Israel has described as a "secret" meeting in the UAE during the war between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Emirati President Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan -- a visit Abu Dhabi denied took place. FRANCE 24's Noga Tarnopolsky reports from Jerusalem.

item.title: Israel-Lebanon ceasefire nears end: Will fresh talks lead to new truce?
item.description: Israel's ruling coalition on Wednesday submitted a proposal to dissolve parliament to pave the way for early elections. The move, initiated by Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party, came as Netanyahu appeared to be facing a possible collapse of his fractious coalition, amid mounting pressure from the ultra-Orthodox parties. item.title: Non-Jewish professor says he was fired for calling out Hamas supporters in online post
item.description: Canadian professor Paul Finlayson says he was fired for defending Israel on social media amid a wave of antisemitism following the Oct. 7 attacks.

item.title: Israel launches fresh strikes on Lebanon despite ceasefire and ongoing talks
item.description: The conflict between Israel and Hezbollah is continuing despite talks currently taking place between Lebanon and Israel. On Wednesday, twelve people were killed by Israeli strikes on Lebanon, according to the country's health ministry. Story by James Vasina.

item.title: Saudi Arabia and U.A.E. Carried Out Secret Attacks in Iran, U.S. Officials Say
item.description: The Gulf Arab states have been grappling with how to deter Iran after the war made clear the limits of American security guarantees.

item.title: ‘These are our people.’ Lebanon’s medics carry on through grief, injuries.
item.description: As Israel and Hezbollah exchange fire, dozens of volunteers eat, sleep and pray at a small hospital, waiting to respond to the next airstrike.

item.title: Iran Lets Chinese Ships Through Strait of Hormuz Amid Rising Tensions After Vessel Seizure
item.description: Iranian news agencies said some Chinese ships were being allowed through the strait, following diplomatic outreach to Iran from Beijing.

item.title: Trump reveals Xi’s stance on arming Iran as Hormuz tensions rattle markets
item.description: President Donald Trump says Chinese President Xi Jinping pledged not to supply Iran with military equipment, calling it a major win from the bilateral summit.
